sister_company_policy.note: Plumbing-vertical extension. Some plumbing clients operate alongside a disclosed sister company (typically a water damage restoration firm: the plumber fixes the pipe, the sister company handles drying and rebuild). This policy governs EXTERNAL cross-links to that sister company; it does not add internal-link kinds above.
sister_company_policy.brand_field: brand.sister_company — OPTIONAL object in plan-input.json's brand block: {"name": "...", "url": "https://...", "relationship": "..."} (relationship is a short human phrase, e.g. "sister company" or "our restoration division").
when_present: Content MAY reference the sister company on water-damage-adjacent topics only: burst pipes, slab leaks, sewer backups, water heater floods, sump pump failures, leak-detection aftermath. Example framing: "if water spread beyond the pipe, our sister company {name} handles the drying and rebuild."

Maximum 1-2 contextual cross-links to sister_company.url per page, placed inline where the water-damage handoff is genuinely relevant. NEVER sitewide: no header, footer, nav, sidebar, or boilerplate-block placement.
The relationship must be disclosed in the surrounding sentence using the provided relationship phrase. Never present the sister company as an unaffiliated third-party recommendation.
Never claim capabilities FOR the sister company beyond a generic drying/restoration/rebuild handoff. Its certifications, hours, and response times are its own site's claims, not ours.
when_absent: If brand.sister_company is not present in the client's plan-input.json brand block, the client has no disclosed sister company. NEVER invent, imply, or placeholder one.

Water-damage-adjacent topics then end at the plumbing scope (stop the water, fix the pipe) plus neutral advice such as contacting the homeowner's insurer or a qualified restoration professional, with no link and no name.
